name: City Council Meeting
minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Agency,
  Community Development Financing Authority,
  Public Improvement Corporation,
  and Library Board of Trustees*

  March 1, 2010

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Agency, the Community
Development Financing Authority, the Public Improvement Corporation, and the Library Board
of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Pro Tem
Leckness at 5:00 p.m., on March 1, 2010 at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on February 26, 2010, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the
Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Ledesma
  Council Member Schlicht
  Council Member Ury
  Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Absent:  Mayor Kelley

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  Irwin B. Bornstein, Assistant City Manager/Director of Admin. Services
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Ledesma

INVOCATION: Council Member Ury

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference With Real Property Negotiator Pursuant To Government Code Section
  54956.8. Real Property Denoted as Parcel 2 of Tentative Tract Map No. 16877, with
  a common address of 25565 Los Alisos Boulevard, Mission Viejo, California and

City Council Minutes  1  March 1, 2010
   generally situated easterly of the intersection of Jeronimo Road and Los Alisos
  Boulevard in the City of Mission Viejo owned by Target Corporation. CDA
  Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, CDA Executive Director/City Manager; Irwin
  Bornstein, Assistant City Manager; Charles Wilson, Director of Community
  Development; James Williams, Economic Advisor; Celeste Brady, CDA Special
  Counsel; William Curley, III, City Attorney and CDA General Counsel.
  Developer’s Negotiators: Bob Garrison of Lennar Homes of California, Inc., as
  prospective buyer from Target Corporation Roger Grable of Manatt Phelps,
  counsel to Lennar. Under negotiation: Real property interests for affordable
  housing, the price and terms of payment thereof for above-listed Property pursuant
  to Affordable Housing Agreement. Factors Affecting Price and Terms under
  Negotiation: Recorded covenants, Scope and schedule of development of Property
  and Affordable housing requirements. Factors affecting time of payment:
  Conditions to closing, Due diligence period and Schedule of Project Development of
  Affordable Housing.

CS2. Labor Negotiations—The Council Will Provide Direction to its Labor Negotiator
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54957.6. The Parties to the Negotiations Are
  the City and City’s Unrepresented Employees. The City’s Negotiator is Dennis
  Wilberg.

CS3. Conference with City Attorney Concerning One Matter of Pending Litigation
  Pursuant to Government Code Section 54956.9(a). The Litigation is Oso Viejo
  Neighbors Association v. City of Mission Viejo et al. Case Number 30-2009-
  00319861.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Pro Tem Leckness recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The
City Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m. with four Council Members present (Mayor Kelley was
absent).

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that for Closed Session item CS1, final action will be taken
in open session under item 6. For CS2 and CS3, the City Council received reports and provided
direction but there was no reportable action.

PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Recognize Community Services Commissioner Ron Ruef for Being Named
  Outstanding Commissioner for the State by the California Association of Park and
  Recreation Commissioners and Board Members (CAPRCBM) for 2009 and being
  selected President of the CAPRCBM for 2010

City Council Minutes  2  March 1, 2010
   Mayor Pro Tem Leckness presented certificates of commendation to Community
  Services Commissioner Ron Ruef.

P2.  Presentation by Rich Dixon of the U.S. Census Bureau Regarding the Upcoming
  2010 Census

  Rich Dixon, U.S. Census Bureau, discussed the 2010 Census efforts and encouraged
  residents to participate by completing the form and returning it by April 1, 2010.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Larry Maurer, M.V.: asked residents to share their vision of the City and stated that a clearly
defined vision will help those who want to take a more active role in the City’s life.

Bari Russell, Vice President of the Friends of the Mission Viejo Library: announced that the
Friends of the Library recently received a philanthropic donation of over $200,000 and she
expressed the Friends’ gratitude.

Neil Lonsinger, M.V.: discussed his concern with pot holes in the city and asked that more staff
become involved in reporting them, including the Sheriff’s deputies.

Harry Lenczyk, M.V.: prior to spending any money, he requested that the City Council make a
presentation and explain to the residents why the Marguerite Tennis Center expansion is so
desperately needed.

Duaine Griffith, M.V.: complained about a neighbor’s barking dog and stated that he is getting
the run around from the city’s Animal Control department. He noted that the problem has
continued for five months and he pleaded for the Council’s help.

Joe Holtzman, M.V.: announced that Assembly Bill 920 requires utility companies to pay for
extra electricity that consumers feed back into the grid. He encouraged residents who have
installed solar power units to get a form from their utility company so they will be compensated
for the net surplus electricity they generate. He noted that the form must be resubmitted
annually.

Anna T. Boyce, M.V.: announced that there will be a census presentation on March 26, 2010,
from 1:00 to 2:00 p.m. at the Community Center. Residents will learn how to complete the
census form and there will be translators present for those who need help in another language.

Carson Finical, M.V.: asked for an update on the status of the dog park.

City Manager Wilberg provided a brief history of the dog park concept and announced that the
matter will come back to the City Council in April. He suggested that Mr. Finical leave his
contact information so he can be placed on the dog park interest list.

City Council Minutes  3  March 1, 2010
 Lisa Harcrow, M.V.: thanked the City Council for the incredible job they have done noting
median beautification, public art work, the senior center and recreation center improvements, and
the Rose Parade float which resulted in community pride.

Ian Mishkin, Lake Forest: stated that the City Council is doing a great job. He aspires to go into
politics when he is older so his visit to the Council Meeting has been a good learning experience.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Item 2 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate discussion.

Motion made by Council Member Ledesma, seconded by Council Member Ury, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Kelley

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said
  titles which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title
  and further reading waived.

3.  Check Register dated February 5, 2010, in the amount of $681,830.99

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Check Register dated February 12, 2010, in the amount of $731,992.76

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Various Speed Limit Updates

  Adopted Ordinance 10-278 Amending Chapter 12.04.010(d) of the Mission Viejo
  Municipal Code Regarding Prima Facie Speed Limits on Certain Streets.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

OLD BUSINESS

City Council Minutes  4  March 1, 2010
 6.  Affordable Housing Agreement Between Community Development Agency of The
  City of Mission Viejo and Lennar Homes of California, Inc.

  Celeste Brady, Special Counsel to the Community Development Agency, presented the
  staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to (1)
  approve Affordable Housing Agreement (AHA) substantially in the form appended to
  this agenda report and authorize execution and attestation thereof; and (2) authorize CDA
  Executive Director (and authorized designees), the CDA General Counsel (City
  Attorney), and CDA Special Counsel to implement the AHA including the following
  actions: execute documents necessary to carry out the Project, make technical or minor
  changes and interpretations to the AHA, if necessary; cause issuance of warrants in
  implementation of the AHA; and administer the CDA?s obligations, responsibilities and
  duties to be performed thereunder.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

NEW BUSINESS

6A.  2009-10 Supplemental Education Revenue Augmentation Fund (SERAF) Payment

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Administrative Services Irwin Bornstein presented
  the staff report.

  Motion made by Council Member Ury, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to (1)
  adopt CDA Resolution 10-01 Approving the Borrowing From its Low and Moderate
  Income Housing Fund For the Purpose of Paying the CDA’s Supplemental Educational
  Revenue Augmentation Fund (SERAF) Payment For Fiscal Year 2009-10 and Making
  Certain Findings Pursuant to Health and Safety Code Section 33690, and (2) adopt
  Resolution 10-12 Approving the Borrowing by the Community Development Agency of
  the City of Mission Viejo From its Low and Moderate Income Housing Fund For the
  Purpose of Paying the CDA’s Supplemental Educational Revenue Augmentation Fund
  (SERAF) Payment for Fiscal Year 2009-10.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

City Council Minutes  5  March 1, 2010
 7.  Appointments to the Community Services Commission, Investment Advisory
  Commission, and the Planning and Transportation Commission by Newly Elected
  Council Member Leckness

  Motion made by Pro Tem Leckness, seconded by Council Member Ledesma, to appoint
  the current Commissioners to serve the remainder of their term: senior member of the
  Community Services Commission Helen Workun, Community Services Commissioner
  Ron Ruef, Investment Advisory Commissioner Matthew Conrad, and Planning and
  Transportation Commissioner Rick Sandzimier.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

2.  City Council Minutes

  Council Member Schlicht expressed concern that the last sentence of her Council
  Comments seemed a little offensive in the Minutes and that was not her intention. She
  had meant to share part of her philosophy which is "better government through public
  participation, public disclosure, public consent and if you're responsible for others make
  sure you do what is right and fair."

  Motion made by Council Member Schlicht, seconded by Council Member Ury, to
  approve the Minutes from the Regular City Council Meeting of February 15, 2010, as
  presented.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Leckness, Ledesma, Schlicht, and Ury
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT: Kelley

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, AND COMMITTEE REPORTS

8.  Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA) Report

  There was no report in Mayor Kelley's absence.

9.  Foothill/Eastern Transportation Corridor Agency Report

City Council Minutes  6  March 1, 2010
   Council Member Ury announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the
  Foothill/Eastern TCA so there was nothing to report.

10.  San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agency Report

  Council Member Ury announced that there has not been a recent meeting of the San
  Joaquin Hills TCA so there was nothing to report.

STAFF REPORTS

City Manager’s Report

11.  Update on Dial-a-Taxi Contract Renewal

  City Manager Wilberg advised the Council that the city has been approached by the City
  of Laguna Hills to explore the opportunity of coordinating senior citizen Dial-a-Taxi
  programs between the two cities. He stated that there are a number of benefits to
  synchronizing transportation and it would allow seniors to get to medical appointments or
  to shop in the adjacent city. Mr. Wilberg advised the Council that staff is beginning
  discussions with Laguna Hills and Council Members can contact him or Recreation and
  Community Services staff if they would like further information.

City Attorney's Report

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS

12.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

  The City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the staff report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the
  public record.

Council Member Ledesma

Council Member Ledesma suggested that the meeting be closed in honor of the former resident
who gave a large donation to the Friends of the Library.

Council Member Schlicht

Council Member Schlicht thanked staff for changing the Youth Athletic Park sign. She stated
that Marty Russo was the driving force behind the Youth Athletic Park and she appreciates that
the sign bearing Mr. Russo’s name was installed so quickly. Council Member Schlicht wished
the Welsh members of the community a happy Saint David’s Day.

City Council Minutes  7  March 1, 2010
 Council Member Ury

13.  Update on Ballot Argument against the Right to Vote Initiative

  Council Member Ury distributed a copy of his argument against the Right to Vote
  Initiative.

Council Member Ury announced that the Santa Margarita Eagles girls’ basketball team made the
CIF championships. He noted that the team includes Mission Viejo residents and his own
daughter and he wished them the best of luck. Council Member Ury acknowledged that some of
the little league opening day games were postponed due to rain and he looks forward to the
games taking place this coming weekend.

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness

Mayor Pro Tem Leckness thanked his colleagues for making him feel comfortable as the new
Council Member and he thanked the residents who have contacted him with support. He
announced that the Rotary Club has an upcoming Spring Fiesta fundraiser at Cafe Maiz on
March 20, 2010, at 6:30 p.m. and he encouraged residents to attend.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:35 p.m., there being no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Pro Tem Leckness adjourned the meeting to Monday, March 15, 2010, at 5:00
p.m.

__________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of March 15, 2010

City Council Minutes  8  March 1, 2010
